law_claim: L1.47 (discrete funding settlement) + R0021 (FR is a quantized transform of PI) + L1.57 (denominator declared)
purpose: Disposition of the past-due [§33: deferred(2026-08-11)] premium-index axis: measure how much information the settled funding print destroys, before paying for any ingest.

SCANNED_denominator.NOTE: 10 symbols is a SMALL denominator and is declared, not hidden (L1.57).

SCANNED_denominator.note: BTCDOMUSDT excluded (synthetic index product, not a normal perp)

live_cross_section.snapshot_caveat: ONE INSTANT, not a time series. Shares are point-in-time.

tie_break_test.caveat: (mark-index)/index is the CURRENT premium, a PROXY for the window-averaged premium index that actually sets funding. Dispersion is concentrated in thin names where the desk has been burned on fees/capacity -- the tie-break is real information, NOT automatically tradeable.

clamp_positive_control.method: 1m premiumIndexKlines averaged over [T-8h,T) vs settled fundingRate at T; fundingTime carries +1ms so the settled rate belongs to the PRECEDING window (alignment declared, L1.46).
clamp_positive_control.residual_misses_explained: Binance uses an impact/time-weighted average over the window; a plain mean of 1m PI closes is an approximation, so a minority of windows miss the 2e-5 tolerance. The model is VERIFIED, not assumed.
clamp_positive_control.formula: F = P + clamp(I - P, +/-0.05%); dead band P in [I-0.05%, I+0.05%] collapses to F = I exactly.

instrument_defect_found_in_my_own_run: First pass counted only the two tie constants I EXPECTED (0.0001, 0.0) and reported 35.5% tied. Reading the actual distribution found a THIRD constant (0.00005, n=270, the 4h-interval dead band) and the true figure is 68.8%. Recorded because it is the L1.57 hardcoded-denominator defect in miniature: I asked how many matched my constants instead of what the distribution looked like.
